item.title: AI has solved many math problems, but it has not solved math | Science
item.description: This summer has featured an amazing run of mathematical discoveries. In May, a prediction first made by Paul Erdős in 1946 about “unit distances” between points in a plane, was disproved. In July, the Jacobian conjecture, an 87-year-old open question in algebraic geometry, was refuted in dimension three. In August, the question of whether a six-dimensional sphere can be given smooth complex coordinates, first asked by Heinz Hopf in 1947, was finally confirmed to be true. Most recently, a finite-time singularity among the solutions to the famous Navier-Stokes equations—a system of equations governing the flow of fluids—was discovered after many decades (in a setting where the fluid is stirred by an external force).

item.title: Climate policies neglect risks posed by legacy landfills | Science
item.description: The environmental hazards associated with legacy landfills can be devastating, and the risks are being intensified by climate change. In August, extreme overnight precipitation compromised the structuralintegrity of the Dar es Salam landfill in Guinea, which had been scheduled to close, causing a landslide that buried homes and killed at least 30 people (1). Earlier this summer, in July, extreme dry-season heat ignited methane pockets in Indonesia’s Jatiwaringin landfill, a legacy open dump, sparking a 10-day fire across 15 hectares (2).

item.title: Careful governance is needed to balance the benefits and risks of landfill mining in China | Science
item.description: In recent years, dozens of Chinese cities across the Yangtze and Pearl River deltas have launched large-scale landfill mining, a process that entails sealed, decades-old municipal waste landfills being excavated and their contents being sorted and combusted in waste-to-energy plants (1, 2). Driven by shrinking fresh combustible waste after mandatory waste classification and overbuilt incineration capacity, this emerging practice delivers tangible socioeconomic and environmental gains yet carries overlooked ecological risks that demand balanced governance (3).
